records.source: רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה פִּצְחִ֨י רִנָּ֤ה וְצַהֲלִי֙ לֹא־חָ֔לָה כִּֽי־רַבִּ֧ים בְּֽנֵי־שׁוֹמֵמָ֛ה מִבְּנֵ֥י בְעוּלָ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Shout for joy, O barren [woman who] has not given birth; break forth [into] a shout of joy and cry aloud, [you who] have not been in labor; for many [are the] children of [the] desolate [woman] more than [the] children of [the] married [woman], says Yahweh.
pieces: Sing out, childless woman who never bore a child; \q burst into song and shout, you who never went into labor! \q For the woman left alone will have more children than the woman who has a husband, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.1: Shout for joy, barren one [who] has not given birth; \q break out [into] a shout of joy and cry aloud, [you who] have not been in labor! \q For the children of the desolate [woman are] more than the children of the married [woman], says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.1: Jerusalem, you are like a woman who could never have children. But now sing and shout for joy! \q You never felt the pains of giving birth, yet you will have more children than a woman who lives with her husband. \q This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says.

decisions.choice: the barren one: Zion, the city pictured as a wife and mother
decisions.reason: The feminine forms continue the address to Zion and Jerusalem in 49:14-21, 51:17-52:2. A city was pictured as a mother and its people as her children; a childless wife was pitied and often shamed (Genesis 30:1, 23; 1 Samuel 1:6). Sarah, the barren mother of the nation, stands behind the picture (51:2).

decisions.choice: the verse is quoted in Galatians 4:27
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this verse in its Greek form to speak of the Jerusalem above, the mother of all who believe, whose children outnumber those of the earthly city.

decisions.choice: desolate ... married: the woman left alone and the woman who has a husband
decisions.reason: The first word is used of land and cities laid waste (49:8, 19); here it pictures a wife left alone, set against a wife who has a husband. The deserted city will have more people than it had before the exile.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem, you are like a woman who could never have children
decisions.reason: Readable names the city being addressed and says the picture is a comparison, as 51:17 and 52:1-2 name Jerusalem and Zion.

decisions.choice: childless woman
decisions.reason: Balanced says what barrenness meant in plain words, as the next line does ("never bore a child").

records.heading: The childless wife will have many children

records.source: הַרְחִ֣יבִי׀מְק֣וֹם אָהֳלֵ֗ךְ וִירִיע֧וֹת מִשְׁכְּנוֹתַ֛יִךְ יַטּ֖וּ אַל־תַּחְשֹׂ֑כִי הַאֲרִ֨יכִי֙ מֵֽיתָרַ֔יִךְ וִיתֵדֹתַ֖יִךְ חַזֵּֽקִי׃
records.gloss: Make wide [the] place of your tent, and [the] curtains of your dwellings let them stretch out; do not hold back; make long your cords, and your pegs make strong.
pieces: Make room in your tent; let the curtains of your dwellings be spread wide, and hold nothing back. \q Let out your tent ropes \q and drive your pegs in firmly.

L.2: Enlarge the place of your tent, and let them stretch out the curtains of your dwellings; do not hold back; \q lengthen your cords, \q and make your pegs strong.

R.2: Make your tent bigger! Spread out its curtains as far as they will go. Do not hold back. \q Make the ropes longer, \q and drive the tent pegs in deep.

decisions.choice: tent, curtains, cords, pegs: a family enlarging its home for more children
decisions.reason: Israel's ancestors lived in tents, and a growing household needed a bigger one. Zion is told to make room for the children promised in verse 1. Compare 33:20, where Zion is a tent whose pegs will never be pulled up.

decisions.choice: let them stretch out: others will help spread the curtains
decisions.reason: The verb is plural and impersonal ("let them stretch"), while the other commands are addressed to Zion herself. The sense is the same: the curtains are to be spread wide.

records.source: כִּי־יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹ֖אול תִּפְרֹ֑צִי וְזַרְעֵךְ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם יִירָ֔שׁ וְעָרִ֥ים נְשַׁמּ֖וֹת יוֹשִֽׁיבוּ׃
records.gloss: For right and left you will spread out, and your offspring nations will dispossess, and cities desolated they will make inhabited.
pieces: For you will burst out to the right and to the left; \q your descendants will take over the lands of nations \q and fill ruined cities with people again.

L.3: For [to the] right and [to the] left you will spread out, \q and your offspring will dispossess nations, \q and they will make desolate cities inhabited.

R.3: Your family will grow and spread out in every direction. \q Your descendants will take over the lands of other nations. \q They will bring people back to live in cities that are now empty.

decisions.choice: you will spread out to the right and left: the promise to Jacob
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in God's promise to Jacob that his offspring would spread out west and east, north and south (Genesis 28:14). "Right and left" means south and north to someone facing east, and so in all directions.

decisions.choice: dispossess: take possession of land in place of those who held it
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of Israel taking the land of Canaan (Deuteronomy 9:1). Compare Genesis 22:17, where Abraham's offspring will possess the gate of their enemies.

decisions.choice: in every direction
decisions.reason: Readable says what "to the right and to the left" means.

records.source: אַל־תִּֽירְאִי֙ כִּי־לֹ֣א תֵב֔וֹשִׁי וְאַל־תִּכָּלְמִ֖י כִּ֣י לֹ֣א תַחְפִּ֑ירִי כִּ֣י בֹ֤שֶׁת עֲלוּמַ֨יִךְ֙ תִּשְׁכָּ֔חִי וְחֶרְפַּ֥ת אַלְמְנוּתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֥א תִזְכְּרִי־עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: Do not be afraid, for not you will be put to shame, and do not be humiliated, for not you will be disgraced; for [the] shame of your youth you will forget, and [the] reproach of your widowhood not you will remember again.
pieces: Have no fear; you will not be put to shame. \q Do not hang your head; no disgrace will come to you. \q You will forget the shame you bore when young \q and no longer call to mind the scorn you suffered as a widow.

L.4: Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; \q and do not be humiliated, for you will not be disgraced; \q for you will forget the shame of your youth, \q and the reproach of your widowhood you will not remember again.

R.4: Do not be afraid. People will not make fun of you anymore. \q Do not feel ashamed, because you will not be disgraced. \q You will forget how ashamed you were when you were young. \q You will not even remember how people looked down on you when you were like a widow.

decisions.choice: the shame of your youth and the reproach of your widowhood: the nation's past disgrace, ended by God's return
decisions.reason: The youth may be the nation's early days of slavery in Egypt or of unfaithfulness (Jeremiah 2:2; Ezekiel 16:22), and the widowhood the exile, when Zion seemed abandoned by her husband (verses 6-7; 49:14). The picture is of a wife who has been through both and now will be restored.

decisions.choice: for ... for ... for: each command not to fear is followed by its reason
decisions.reason: Three clauses begin with the same particle: Zion need not fear, because shame will not come; and the old shame itself will be forgotten.

decisions.choice: how people looked down on you when you were like a widow
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the reproach of your widowhood": the scorn a widow bore, here the city's disgrace while she seemed abandoned.

records.source: כִּ֤י בֹעֲלַ֨יִךְ֙ עֹשַׂ֔יִךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ וְגֹֽאֲלֵךְ֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֱלֹהֵ֥י כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ יִקָּרֵֽא׃
records.gloss: For your husband [is] your Maker, Yahweh of hosts [is] his name; and your Redeemer [is the] Holy One of Israel, [the] God of all the earth he is called.
pieces: Your husband is the one who made you; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. \q Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is called God of the whole earth.

L.5: For your husband [is] your Maker, \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; \q and your Redeemer [is] the Holy One of Israel; \q the God of all the earth {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is called.

R.5: The God who made you will be like a husband to you. \q His name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q The Holy One of Israel will rescue you. \q People call {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the God of the whole earth.

decisions.choice: your husband, your Maker: plural forms that refer to the one God
decisions.reason: Both words are plural in form, as the word for God is, a plural of majesty; the verb and "his name" show that one person is meant.

decisions.choice: your husband is your Maker: the LORD who made Israel binds himself to her as a husband
decisions.reason: The marriage picture of God and his people runs through the prophets (62:4-5; Jeremiah 3:14; Hosea 2:18-22). The one who made the nation (43:1, 7) is the one who takes her back.

decisions.choice: Redeemer: the next of kin who buys back and protects
decisions.reason: A redeemer was the relative who bought back family land or family members and stood up for them (Leviticus 25:25, 47-49; Ruth 4:4-6). Isaiah gives God this title often (41:14; 43:14; 47:4).

decisions.choice: will be like a husband to you; will rescue you
decisions.reason: Readable states the picture as a comparison and says what a redeemer does.

records.source: כִּֽי־כְאִשָּׁ֧ה עֲזוּבָ֛ה וַעֲצ֥וּבַת ר֖וּחַ קְרָאָ֣ךְ יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֧שֶׁת נְעוּרִ֛ים כִּ֥י תִמָּאֵ֖ס אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: For like a wife abandoned and grieved of spirit has called you Yahweh, and a wife of youth when she is rejected, says your God.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} calls to you as to a wife left alone and grieving in spirit, \q as to the wife a man married young and then cast off, says your God.

L.6: For like a wife forsaken and grieved in spirit {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has called you, \q and [like] a wife of youth when she is rejected, says your God.

R.6: You are like a wife whose husband left her and who is deeply sad. \q You are like a young wife whose husband sent her away. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is calling you back to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. This is what your God says.

decisions.choice: when she is rejected: the young wife who has been cast off
decisions.reason: The clause may also be a question: "a wife of youth, can she be rejected?", meaning that a man does not throw away the wife he loved when young. Both readings lead to God taking his wife back.

decisions.choice: has called you: summoned you back as his wife
decisions.reason: The past tense describes what God is doing as already done. He calls the abandoned wife back to himself, as the following verses explain.

decisions.choice: calling you back to himself
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the purpose of the call, which verses 7-8 make clear.

records.source: בְּרֶ֥גַע קָטֹ֖ן עֲזַבְתִּ֑יךְ וּבְרַחֲמִ֥ים גְּדֹלִ֖ים אֲקַבְּצֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: For a moment small I abandoned you, and with compassions great I will gather you.
pieces: I forsook you for a passing moment, \q but with vast compassion I will gather you in.

L.7: For a small moment I forsook you, \q but with great compassion I will gather you.

R.7: For a short time I left you alone. \q But I love you very much, and I will bring you back home.

decisions.choice: a small moment ... great compassion: the exile was brief beside the mercy that follows
decisions.reason: The contrast of small and great sets the time of punishment against the size of God's mercy, as Psalm 30:6 sets a moment of anger against a lifetime of favor.

decisions.choice: gather: bring the scattered people back together
decisions.reason: The verb is used of gathering exiles from the nations (11:12; 43:5; 56:8).

decisions.choice: I love you very much, and I will bring you back home
decisions.reason: Readable puts "great compassion" as tender love and says where the gathering leads.

records.source: בְּשֶׁ֣צֶף קֶ֗צֶף הִסְתַּ֨רְתִּי פָנַ֥י רֶ֨גַע֙ מִמֵּ֔ךְ וּבְחֶ֥סֶד עוֹלָ֖ם רִֽחַמְתִּ֑יךְ אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: In a flood of wrath I hid my face a moment from you, and in loyal love of perpetuity I will have compassion on you, says your Redeemer, Yahweh.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger overflowed, I turned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face away from you for a moment; \q but with loyal love that lasts forever I will show you compassion, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your Redeemer.

L.8: In an overflow of wrath I hid {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from you [for] a moment, \q but with everlasting loyal love I will have compassion on you, \q says your Redeemer, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: I was very angry, and for a short time I turned away from you. \q But my faithful love will last forever, and I will be kind to you. \q This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says, the one who rescues you.

decisions.choice: a flood of wrath: anger that overflowed
decisions.reason: The first word appears only here; it is usually taken as a form of the word for a flood, chosen for its sound beside the word for wrath. The sense is anger poured out for a short time.

decisions.choice: I hid my face: I withdrew my favor and help
decisions.reason: To hide one's face is to turn away and give no help (8:17; 59:2; Deuteronomy 31:17-18).

decisions.choice: everlasting loyal love: covenant faithfulness without end
decisions.reason: The word is the faithful love that keeps a covenant (55:3; Exodus 34:6-7). It is set against the short moment of anger.

decisions.choice: I will be kind to you
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what showing compassion means here.

records.source: כִּי־מֵ֥י נֹ֨חַ֙ זֹ֣את לִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבַּ֗עְתִּי מֵעֲבֹ֥ר מֵי־נֹ֛חַ ע֖וֹד עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כֵּ֥ן נִשְׁבַּ֛עְתִּי מִקְּצֹ֥ף עָלַ֖יִךְ וּמִגְּעָר־בָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: For [the] waters of Noah this [is] to me, which I swore from passing [the] waters of Noah again over the earth; so I swear from being angry toward you and from rebuking you.
pieces: This is for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as it was with the waters of Noah. \q Just as I took an oath that Noah's flood would never again sweep over the earth, \q so I take an oath now: I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.

L.9: For this [is like] the waters of Noah to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: \q as I swore that the waters of Noah would not pass over the earth again, \q so I swear that [I will] not be angry with you or rebuke you.

R.9: This is like what happened in the time of Noah. \q After the great flood, I promised that a flood would never cover the earth again. \q In the same way, I now promise that I will not be angry with you. I will not punish you again.

decisions.choice: the waters of Noah: God's oath after the flood
decisions.reason: After the flood God promised that waters would never again destroy the earth, and set the rainbow as the sign of that covenant (Genesis 8:21-22; 9:11-17). His promise to Zion is as firm as that one.

decisions.choice: for the waters of Noah: the word division of the standard Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The same letters divided differently read "like the days of Noah". Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions are reported to read it that way; the sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: I swear: the oath is made in the speaking
decisions.reason: The verb has the same form as "I swore" before it, but here it states an oath God makes as he speaks, matched to the oath of Noah's day.

records.heading: A promise as firm as the oath to Noah

records.source: כִּ֤י הֶֽהָרִים֙ יָמ֔וּשׁוּ וְהַגְּבָע֖וֹת תְּמוּטֶ֑נָה וְחַסְדִּ֞י מֵאִתֵּ֣ךְ לֹֽא־יָמ֗וּשׁ וּבְרִ֤ית שְׁלוֹמִי֙ לֹ֣א תָמ֔וּט אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: For the mountains will be removed, and the hills will shake, and my loyal love from with you not will be removed, and [the] covenant of my peace not will shake, says [the one] having compassion on you, Yahweh.
pieces: The mountains may move away \q and the hills may totter, \q yet {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} loyal love will never move away from you, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant of peace will not totter, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who shows you compassion.

L.10: For the mountains may depart, \q and the hills may shake, \q but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} loyal love will not depart from you, and the covenant of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} peace will not shake, \q says the one who has compassion on you, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: Even if the mountains disappear \q and the hills are shaken, \q my faithful love for you will never go away. My promise of peace to you will never be shaken. \q This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says, who is so kind to you.

decisions.choice: for the mountains may depart: a concession, even if the most lasting things give way
decisions.reason: The mountains and hills are the firmest things in creation (Psalm 46:3-4; Habakkuk 3:6). Even if they were removed, God's love would stay. The two verbs, depart and shake, are repeated for his love and his covenant.

decisions.choice: my covenant of peace: God's binding promise of well-being and safety
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of God's covenant with Phinehas (Numbers 25:12) and of the covenant he will make with his restored people (Ezekiel 34:25; 37:26). Peace here is wholeness and security.

decisions.choice: my promise of peace
decisions.reason: Readable explains a covenant as a binding promise.

records.source: עֲנִיָּ֥ה סֹעֲרָ֖ה לֹ֣א נֻחָ֑מָה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַרְבִּ֤יץ בַּפּוּךְ֙ אֲבָנַ֔יִךְ וִיסַדְתִּ֖יךְ בַּסַּפִּירִֽים׃
records.gloss: O afflicted [one], storm-tossed, not comforted, here, I [am] setting in antimony your stones, and I will found you with sapphires.
pieces: Poor wretched city, battered by storms and left without comfort, \q look: I will set your stones in dark mortar \q and lay your foundations with sapphires.

L.11: Afflicted one, storm-tossed, not comforted, \q look, I am setting your stones in antimony, \q and I will lay your foundations with sapphires.

R.11: Jerusalem, you have suffered so much. You have been battered like a ship in a storm, and no one has comforted you. \q But look! I will rebuild you with beautiful stones. \q I will build your foundations with precious blue stones.

decisions.choice: antimony: the black mineral used as eye paint, here a dark setting for the stones
decisions.reason: The word names eye paint in 2 Kings 9:30 and colored stone in 1 Chronicles 29:2. Here it is probably a dark mortar that makes the stones stand out, as paint sets off the eyes. The exact sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: sapphires: a costly blue stone, probably lapis lazuli
decisions.reason: The ancient stone of this name was deep blue (Exodus 24:10; Ezekiel 1:26). It was probably lapis lazuli rather than the modern sapphire. Many of the stone names in verses 11-12 cannot be identified with certainty.

decisions.choice: a city built of precious stones
decisions.reason: The rebuilt city is pictured with jewels for walls and foundations. Revelation 21:18-21 takes up the picture for the new Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem; battered like a ship in a storm
decisions.reason: Readable names the city addressed (see verse 1) and explains "storm-tossed" as a comparison.

records.heading: A city built of precious stones

records.source: וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י כַּֽדְכֹד֙ שִׁמְשֹׁתַ֔יִךְ וּשְׁעָרַ֖יִךְ לְאַבְנֵ֣י אֶקְדָּ֑ח וְכָל־גְּבוּלֵ֖ךְ לְאַבְנֵי־חֵֽפֶץ׃
records.gloss: And I will make [of] ruby your battlements, and your gates [of] stones of beryl, and all your border [of] stones of delight.
pieces: I will crown your towers with rubies, \q build your gates of fiery gems, \q and make your whole outer wall of costly stones.

L.12: And I will make your battlements [of] rubies, \q and your gates [of] sparkling stones, \q and all your boundary [of] precious stones.

R.12: I will decorate the tops of your towers with red jewels. \q I will make your gates out of shining jewels. \q I will make the wall all around you out of precious stones.

decisions.choice: battlements: literally "your suns", the parts of the wall that catch the sunlight
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "sun". It probably names the tops of the walls or towers that gleam in the sun.

decisions.choice: ruby and sparkling stones: red or glowing gems whose exact identity is unknown
decisions.reason: The first word appears only here and in Ezekiel 27:16 among goods of trade; it is a red stone, perhaps ruby or agate. The second comes from a verb meaning to kindle, so a stone that glows like fire, perhaps garnet or carbuncle.

decisions.choice: your boundary: the wall that marks the city's border
decisions.reason: The word means border or territory; with stones it means the outer wall around the city.

records.source: וְכָל־בָּנַ֖יִךְ לִמּוּדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְרַ֖ב שְׁל֥וֹם בָּנָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And all your children [will be] taught [ones] of Yahweh, and great [will be the] peace of your children.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will teach every one of your children, \q and great peace will be theirs.

L.13: And all your children [will be] taught by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and great [will be] the peace of your children.

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will teach all your children, \q and they will enjoy great peace.

decisions.choice: taught by the LORD: disciples, people who have learned from God
decisions.reason: The word means one who is taught, a disciple (8:16; 50:4). Jesus quotes this line in John 6:45 to say that those who learn from the Father come to him.

decisions.choice: your children: the standard Hebrew text repeats the word
decisions.reason: The same letters can be read as "your builders". The rabbis made a wordplay on this (Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 64a), and the Great Isaiah Scroll may have that reading; it fits the building picture of verses 11-12. The standard text reads "your children" twice.

records.source: בִּצְדָקָ֖ה תִּכּוֹנָ֑נִי רַחֲקִ֤י מֵעֹ֨שֶׁק֙ כִּֽי־לֹ֣א תִירָ֔אִי וּמִ֨מְּחִתָּ֔ה כִּ֥י לֹֽא־תִקְרַ֖ב אֵלָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: In righteousness you will be established; be far from oppression, for not you will fear, and from terror, for not it will draw near to you.
pieces: You will be set firm in righteousness. \q Stay far from oppression, for you will have nothing to fear, \q and from terror, for it will not draw near you.

L.14: In righteousness you will be established; \q be far from oppression, for you will not fear, \q and from terror, for it will not come near you.

R.14: I will make you strong and secure through righteousness. \q No one will be cruel to you, so you will have nothing to be afraid of. \q Nothing terrible will come near you.

decisions.choice: in righteousness: by God's saving justice, which sets things right
decisions.reason: Righteousness in these chapters is often God's faithful action that puts his people in the right and rescues them (46:13; 51:5-6). The city will stand on that foundation.

decisions.choice: be far from oppression: a command used as a promise
alternatives: you will be far from oppression
decisions.reason: The imperative states what will be: oppression will be far away. The reasons that follow ("for you will not fear") show it is a promise more than a duty.

decisions.choice: No one will be cruel to you
decisions.reason: Readable turns the command into the promise it expresses and explains oppression.

records.source: הֵ֣ן גּ֥וֹר יָג֛וּר אֶ֖פֶס מֵֽאוֹתִ֑י מִי־גָ֥ר אִתָּ֖ךְ עָלַ֥יִךְ יִפּֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: If indeed anyone stirs up strife, not from me; whoever stirs up strife with you, over you will fall.
pieces: Should anyone pick a fight with you, it does not come from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q whoever attacks you will fall before you.

L.15: If anyone indeed stirs up strife, [it is] not from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q whoever stirs up strife with you will fall because of you.

R.15: If anyone attacks you, it is not because I sent them. \q Whoever fights against you will be defeated because of you.

decisions.choice: if: the particle introduces a supposed case
decisions.reason: The word usually means "look", but here, as in Aramaic and in Leviticus 25:20, it introduces a condition.

decisions.choice: stirs up strife: attacks; will fall because of you: will be defeated
alternatives: whoever lives as a foreigner with you will join you
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to attack or to stay as a foreigner. With the second sense the line would say that whoever settles among you will join your side. The setting of verses 14-17 favors attack.

decisions.choice: not from me: God no longer sends enemies against Zion
decisions.reason: In the past God used enemies to punish his people (10:5-6). Now any attack will be against his will and will fail.

records.source: הִנֵּ֤ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ בָּרָ֣אתִי חָרָ֔שׁ נֹפֵ֨חַ֙ בְּאֵ֣שׁ פֶּחָ֔ם וּמוֹצִ֥יא כְלִ֖י לְמַעֲשֵׂ֑הוּ וְאָנֹכִ֛י בָּרָ֥אתִי מַשְׁחִ֖ית לְחַבֵּֽל׃
records.gloss: Here, I created a craftsman blowing on a fire of charcoal and bringing out a weapon for its work; and I created a destroyer to ruin.
pieces: Look: I made the metalworker who blows on the burning charcoal \q and turns out a weapon for its use. \q I also made the one who destroys, to bring ruin.

L.16: Look, I created the smith who blows on the fire of charcoal \q and brings out a weapon for its work; \q and I created the destroyer to ruin.

R.16: Listen! I made the worker who blows on the hot coals and makes weapons. \q I also made the soldier who uses them to destroy.

decisions.choice: look: the reading of the margin (qere)
decisions.reason: The written text (ketiv) has a shorter form of the same word; the margin has the usual form. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: I created the smith and the destroyer: both weapons and their users are under God's control
decisions.reason: The one who forges weapons and the one who wields them are both God's creatures, so no weapon can act against his will. This is the ground of the promise in verse 17.

decisions.choice: the soldier who uses them
decisions.reason: Readable links the destroyer with the weapons just named, which is the point of the verse.

records.source: כָּל־כְּלִ֞י יוּצַ֤ר עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ לֹ֣א יִצְלָ֔ח וְכָל־לָשׁ֛וֹן תָּֽקוּם־אִתָּ֥ךְ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט תַּרְשִׁ֑יעִי זֹ֡את נַחֲלַת֩ עַבְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֧ה וְצִדְקָתָ֛ם מֵאִתִּ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Every weapon formed against you not will succeed, and every tongue rising against you for judgment you will condemn; this [is the] inheritance of [the] servants of Yahweh, and their righteousness from with me, utterance of Yahweh.
pieces: Not one weapon shaped to harm you will succeed, \q and every tongue that accuses you in court you will prove wrong. \q This is the share that belongs to the servants of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; their righteousness comes from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.17: Every weapon [that is] formed against you will not succeed, \q and every tongue [that] rises against you in judgment you will condemn. \q This [is] the inheritance of the servants of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and their righteousness [is] from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.17: No weapon that people make to hurt you will win. \q When people accuse you in court, you will show that they are wrong. \q This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives to those who serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Their righteousness comes from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: inheritance: the share given to each, as land was given to the tribes
decisions.reason: The word is used of each tribe's portion of the land (Joshua 13:14). The servants' portion is God's protection and vindication.

decisions.choice: their righteousness: their vindication, being shown to be in the right
decisions.reason: Set beside the court case in the first half, righteousness here is God declaring his servants in the right against their accusers (50:8-9; 45:24-25).

decisions.choice: the servants of the LORD: for the first time in these chapters, the servant is plural
decisions.reason: After the one servant of 52:13-53:12, the following chapters speak of many servants, the faithful people who share in what he won (56:6; 63:17; 65:8-9, 13-15).
